# GO Feature Flag

> GO Feature Flag is a simple, complete and lightweight self-hosted feature flag solution, 100% open source (MIT) and OpenFeature-native.


## docs

GO Feature Flag documentation — describe your feature flags in a simple configuration file, serve them with the relay proxy, and evaluate them from any OpenFeature SDK.

- [GO Feature Flag documentation](https://gofeatureflag.org/docs.md): GO Feature Flag documentation — describe your feature flags in a simple configuration file, serve them with the relay proxy, and evaluate them from any OpenFeature SDK.

### category

- [GO module](https://gofeatureflag.org/docs/category/go-module.md)

### concepts

- [🏗️ Architecture](https://gofeatureflag.org/docs/concepts/architecture.md): What is the GO Feature Flag architecture
- [🔎 Evaluation Context](https://gofeatureflag.org/docs/concepts/evaluation-context.md): An evaluation context in a feature flagging system is crucial for determining the output of a feature flag evaluation. It's a collection of pertinent data about the conditions under which the evaluation is being made.
- [🚚 Exporter](https://gofeatureflag.org/docs/concepts/exporter.md): Exporter are used to export your evaluation data to a remote source.
- [🚥 Flag Evaluation](https://gofeatureflag.org/docs/concepts/flag-evaluation.md): Flag evaluation dynamically determines a feature flag's state at runtime based on context and targeting rules.
- [⛳️ Flag Set](https://gofeatureflag.org/docs/concepts/flagset.md): Flag sets are a powerful feature in GO Feature Flag that allows you to organize your feature flags into separate groups, each with its own configuration, API keys, retrievers, exporters, and notifiers.
- [📣 Notifier](https://gofeatureflag.org/docs/concepts/notifier.md): Notifier are used to notified external systems that a flag configuration has changed.
- [🎣 Retriever](https://gofeatureflag.org/docs/concepts/retriever.md): Retrievers are used to fetch the feature flag configuration from a remote source.
- [🧩 SDK paradigms](https://gofeatureflag.org/docs/concepts/sdk-paradigms.md): GO Feature Flag can be use in the server and client side, check the differences.

### configure_flag

- [🆕 Create Flags](https://gofeatureflag.org/docs/configure_flag/create-flags.md): What is a flag and how you can create them.
- [🪣 Custom Bucketing](https://gofeatureflag.org/docs/configure_flag/custom-bucketing.md): How to bucket users based on a custom identifier
- [🚀 Rollouts](https://gofeatureflag.org/docs/configure_flag/rollout-strategies.md): Choose the right rollout for your feature flag.
- [📊 Experimentation rollout](https://gofeatureflag.org/docs/configure_flag/rollout-strategies/experimentation.md): An experimentation rollout is when your flag is configured to be served only for a determined time.
- [💯 Percentage rollout](https://gofeatureflag.org/docs/configure_flag/rollout-strategies/percentage.md): A percentage rollout refers to a gradual release of a new feature to a subset of users.
- [📈 Progressive rollout](https://gofeatureflag.org/docs/configure_flag/rollout-strategies/progressive.md): A progressive rollout refers to an automated gradual release of a new feature.
- [⏱️ Scheduled rollout](https://gofeatureflag.org/docs/configure_flag/rollout-strategies/scheduled.md): Scheduled rollout introduces the ability for users to changes their flags for future points in time.
- [🎯 Target with Flags](https://gofeatureflag.org/docs/configure_flag/target-with-flags.md): How to create a rule to target specific users

### relay-proxy

GO Feature Flag Relay Proxy is a powerful tool that allows developers to easily integrate feature flagging functionality into their applications. It is a simple API service that can be called directly through the API or via the available OpenFeature providers. The service wraps the GO Feature Flag golang module to evaluate your flags and allows it to be used with all the available languages.

- [↔️ Relay proxy](https://gofeatureflag.org/docs/relay-proxy.md): GO Feature Flag Relay Proxy is a powerful tool that allows developers to easily integrate feature flagging functionality into their applications. It is a simple API service that can be called directly through the API or via the available OpenFeature providers. The service wraps the GO Feature Flag golang module to evaluate your flags and allows it to be used with all the available languages.
- [‼️ Advanced usage](https://gofeatureflag.org/docs/relay-proxy/advanced_usage.md): All the advanced usage of the relay proxy.
- [🔧 Configuration](https://gofeatureflag.org/docs/relay-proxy/configure-relay-proxy.md): How to configure the relay proxy to serve your feature flags.
- [🚀 Deployment](https://gofeatureflag.org/docs/relay-proxy/deployment.md): How to deploy GO Feature Flag relay proxy in different environments.
- [.NET Aspire](https://gofeatureflag.org/docs/relay-proxy/deployment/aspire.md): How to run the GO Feature Flag relay proxy from a .NET Aspire AppHost.
- [AWS Lambda](https://gofeatureflag.org/docs/relay-proxy/deployment/aws-lambda.md): How to deploy GO Feature Flag relay proxy inside a AWS Lambda.
- [Helm](https://gofeatureflag.org/docs/relay-proxy/deployment/helm.md): How to deploy GO Feature Flag relay proxy with Helm.
- [🏁 Getting started](https://gofeatureflag.org/docs/relay-proxy/getting_started.md): Getting started with the relay proxy.
- [🛠️ Installation](https://gofeatureflag.org/docs/relay-proxy/install_relay_proxy.md): Relay proxy is the component that will evaluate the flags, this page explain how to install it.
- [👀 Observability](https://gofeatureflag.org/docs/relay-proxy/observability.md): Logging, Monitoring and Tracing of the relay proxy.
- [📈 Profiling](https://gofeatureflag.org/docs/relay-proxy/profiling.md): Profiling of the relay proxy.
- [🌐 API endpoints](https://gofeatureflag.org/docs/relay-proxy/relay_proxy_endpoints.md): Description of the available endpoints in the relay proxy.

- [(Java) OpenFeature provider improve the internal cache management.](https://gofeatureflag.org/blog/2024/10/20/breaking-change-java.md): The Java provider has been updated to improve the internal cache management by migrating from guava cache to caffeine cache.

### 2025

- [Introducing Exporter Metadata in the GO Feature Flag Provider for OpenFeature.](https://gofeatureflag.org/blog/2025/01/21/exporter-metadata.md): Exporter metadata in the GO Feature Flag provider for OpenFeature allows enriching evaluation events with static context data like environment or app version for improved observability and analysis.
- [Watch Thomas's PlatformCon 2025 Talk on Feature Flag Decoupling](https://gofeatureflag.org/blog/2025/07/01/platformcon-2025-talk.md): Thomas Poignant presents "Decouple Deployments and Releases with OpenFeature" at PlatformCon 2025, exploring how to separate feature releases from code deployments using feature flags and OpenFeature.
- [🏗️ Introducing Flag Sets: Organize Your Feature Flags Like Never Before](https://gofeatureflag.org/blog/2025/09/18/introducing-flagsets.md): Discover how GO Feature Flag's new flag sets feature enables better organization, team isolation, and multi-tenant support for your feature flag management.
- [Grafana is Now Using GO Feature Flag 🎉](https://gofeatureflag.org/blog/2025/10/03/grafana-using-go-feature-flag.md): We’re proud to announce that Grafana, one of the world’s most popular observability platforms, is now using GO Feature Flag as a dependency in their project! 🚀

### 2026

- [In-Process Evaluation for GO Feature Flag OpenFeature Providers](https://gofeatureflag.org/blog/2026/03/31/in-process-openfeature-providers.md): GO, Java, .NET, Python, and JavaScript/TypeScript providers now support in-process evaluation for faster flag resolution with far fewer network calls.

### introduction-blog-post

I absolutely don’t think human/manual QA gates should be involved in between the writing of code and its being live. To avoid breaking things every time and to have an early cutoff system, you should use feature flags.

- [Introduction blog post](https://gofeatureflag.org/blog/introduction-blog-post.md): I absolutely don’t think human/manual QA gates should be involved in between the writing of code and its being live. To avoid breaking things every time and to have an early cutoff system, you should use feature flags.

### solaris-go-feature-flag-case-study

Why a German Banking-as-a-Service provider retired its in-house toggle system for GO Feature Flag, after weighing it against seven alternatives under hard EU data residency and zero-budget constraints.
